history.dynasty: Chola (an inscription records a visit by a Chola king named Janamejaya in the 11th century; Mysore records place the temple a few centuries old)
history.period: Medieval origins; Chola-era inscription dated to the 11th century; current administration under the Karnataka Department of Religious Endowment
history.summary: The Sri Prasanna Venkateswara Temple at Chikka Tirupati is called 'Mini Tirupati' because its customs and traditions follow those of the Tirupati Venkateswara temple exactly, and devotees hold a vow or tonsure here as equal to one at Tirupati. The temple is built in Dravidian architecture with a 5-tiered gopuram and a 70-foot wooden chariot used to carry the Utsavamurthy during Brahmotsava. The exact founding date is unknown; Mysore records indicate the temple is a few centuries old, and an inscription records a visit by a Chola king named Janamejaya in the 11th century. It is now administered by the Department of Religious Endowment, Government of Karnataka. NOTE: the CSV lists the town as 'Kolar', but the temple stands in the town of Chikka Tirupati in Malur taluk of Kolar district, about 40 km from Bengaluru; the town field here records Chikka Tirupati. Opening hours differ across sources (one lists 8 AM-12 noon and 5:30-8:30 PM; another lists 8 AM-7 PM with four daily rituals) - verify before visiting.

name: Chikka Tirupati Temple
town_description: Chikka Tirupati is a small temple town in Malur taluk of Kolar district, Karnataka, about 40 km from Bengaluru on NH-648 (old NH-207) between Bengaluru and Malur, near the rock-sculpture village of Shivarapatna.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru, about 68 km via Hoskote; the temple is about 25 km from Hoskote.
travel.railway: Malur railway station, about 18 km away.
travel.road: On NH-648 between Bengaluru and Malur in Kolar district, about 40 km from Bengaluru; reachable via Old Airport Road and NH-207 (Hoskote route).

visitor_information.best_time: Year-round; the temple is busiest during Brahmotsavam (Shravana) and festival weekends, so early morning darshan is recommended.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 8:00 AM to 12:00 noon and 5:30 PM to 8:30 PM daily in most sources; one source lists 8:00 AM to 7:00 PM with four daily rituals - verify before visiting.
